newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST -- Czech Republic -- Jan 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST -- Czech Republic -- Jan 14.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Automotive corporation Skoda Auto had record sales in 1996 of 261,067 automobiles, which shows an increase of 24.6 percent over 1995. The number of automobiles produced was only a bit higher and amounted to 263,193 vehicles.

- The Czech Republic will pay more than 370 million crowns to the U.N. budget this year for peace operations. Of course, this sum could have been up to three times higher had the U.N. not decided on the Czech share of payment in a meeting in December.
- The increase in prices of advertising services and television and radio commercials this year will not be as dynamic as last year.
LIDOVE NOVINY - Pharmacists have joined general practitioners in threatening to file suit against the Health Ministry for refusing to give credits to insurance companies.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The corporation Harvard Capital & Consulting, which recently announced its intention to transform its closed-end unit trusts into open-end funds, asked yesterday for permission from the Finance Ministry to take this step.

PRAVO - In a meeting Monday of representatives of parliament, senators, members of the board and experts from the Social Democratic Party, the presence of foreign politics spokesman for the German Social Democratic Party Gunter Verghuegen helped the Czech party send a message to Chancellor Helmut Kohl regarding changes in the Czech-German Declaration.

- Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik plans price increases, not just for heating, which was decided previously, but for all energy this summer. Aside from these increases, which are within his power to enforce, Kocarnik wants to present a proposal to the cabinet and the parliament calling for higher tax charges of energy and coal beginning July 1. Prague Newsroom -- 42-2-24-23-0003
